Sam (AE): AegisMed POC frontend is crashing on some streamed completions. They see `Unexpected token \u0000` in JSON.parse.
Priya (Client): repro: open SSE, after a few events one event fails parsing and the UI drops that message. No 500s.
Noel (SE): can you grab raw bytes with `curl -N` and a hex dump? need to confirm stray 0x00.
Priya (Client): ran `curl -N -s https://poc.aegismed/stream > out.bin && xxd -g1 out.bin | sed -n '20,40p'`, snippet: `... 7d 0a 0a 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22id\":\"msg42\"7d 00 0a 0a` — there's a `00` after the JSON object.
Kai (Oncall): 0x00 is the cause. Typical sources: proxy buffering padding (nginx), CDN edge normalization, or an upstream write that pads fixed-size buffers. What sits in front?
Priya (Client): Cloudflare + nginx reverse proxy + internal LB.
Ruth (Eng): we've seen two classes: (A) padding inserted by buffering proxies, (B) partial-event timing where client tries to parse before the terminating blank line arrives. Both can produce parse errors.
Noel (SE): quick triage steps for you: 1) curl -N to capture raw bytes 2) hexdump and search for `00` near `0a 0a` separators 3) try bypassing Cloudflare to see if edge is source.
Priya (Client): bypassed Cloudflare -> the NUL went away in the capture. Edge is likely introducing it.
Kai (Oncall): short-term infra mitigations: on nginx location for the stream set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; gzip off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; sendfile off; proxy_read_timeout 3600;` Also ensure upstream doesn't send Content-Length for streaming responses.
Noel (SE): client-side safety (temporary): accumulate until you see the SSE event delimiter (`\n\n`) and strip NULs before parsing. Minimal Node pattern: `let buf=''; res.on('data',c=>{buf+=c; let i; while((i=buf.indexOf('\n\n'))>-1){const evt=buf.slice(0,i);buf=buf.slice(i+2);const dataLines=evt.split('\n').filter(l=>l.startsWith('data:'));const payload=dataLines.map(l=>l.replace(/^data:\s*/,'' )).join('\n');const clean=payload.replace(/\u0000/g,''); try{JSON.parse(clean);}catch(e){console.warn('parse fail',e,payload)} }});`
Priya (Client): implemented buffer + NUL strip; much more stable.
deploy-bot: Deployed `poc/edge-bypass-test` to staging (build #1180). :white_check_mark:
Ruth (Eng): on Redwood side we can enable `sse-strict-mode=true` for this tenant to guarantee exact event flushing and emit telemetry when we detect padding. Zoe, is it OK to toggle that for the POC?
Zoe (Presales): yes, toggle is fine for POC; document it in the engagement notes.
Kai (Oncall): follow-ups: 1) I'll add an infra blurb for SSE routes (nginx + CDN checklist) to the POC doc, 2) Ruth will open an internal ticket to consider defaulting the strict flag for new POCs and surface padding telemetry.
Noel (SE): also advised AegisMed to inspect app-server writes (avoid preallocated fixed-size buffers, avoid sendfile for dynamic SSE).
Priya (Client): after the client change + Cloudflare bypass the stream has been clean for 20+ hours. Thanks team.
Sam (AE): good swoop. Action items: Kai/Ruth doc infra snippet, Noel/Zoe add the runtime toggle + client workaround to the POC wrap-up. Close once docs linked. :tada:
